title: A gradebook report
description:
Write a program that reads exam results as CSV from standard input and prints a report. The first line is the header `name,subject,score`; each other line is one result:

```
name,subject,score
Ada,maths,92
Bob,maths,61
Ada,art,78
Bob,art,85
Cy,maths,abc
Cy,maths,47
```

prints

```
line 6: bad score 'abc'
Students:
  Ada         85.0 B  (2 results)
  Bob         73.0 C  (2 results)
  Cy          47.0 F  (1 result)
Subjects:
  art        avg 81.5  best Bob (85)
  maths      avg 66.7  best Ada (92)
Errors: 1
```

Rules:
- A wrong header prints `error: bad header` and stops at once. Blank lines are skipped.
- Each line has exactly 3 comma-separated fields, trimmed. Problems are printed **as they are read**, as `line <n>: <message>` (the header is line 1), and the line is skipped: `expected 3 fields`, `empty name`, `empty subject`, `bad score '<text>'` (not a whole number), `score <n> out of range` (not 0 to 100).
- Students are listed by average (highest first), then by name. Each line: two spaces, the name left-aligned in 10 characters, the average right-aligned in 5 with one decimal, a space, the grade (90 `A`, 80 `B`, 70 `C`, 60 `D`, else `F`, using the unrounded average), and `  (<n> results)` (`1 result` for one).
- Subjects are listed by name. Each line: two spaces, the subject left-aligned in 10 characters, ` avg <average with one decimal>`, two spaces, and `best <name> (<score>)` for the highest score (on a tie, the name that sorts first).
- Last, `Errors: <count>`. With no valid results at all, print `No data.` instead of the two lists (but still the errors before it and the count after it).
hints: `let [name, subject, score] = fields[..] else { return Err(...) };` takes a slice apart only when it has exactly three items.
A `BTreeMap<&str, Vec<u32>>` keyed by student gives each student's scores in one place; build a second one keyed by subject that keeps `(name, score)` pairs for finding the best.
`f64` has no total order, so sort averages with `b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap()` (the averages are never NaN) and break ties with `.then_with(|| a.0.cmp(b.0))`.
requirements: A `RowError` enum with a `Display` implementation for the messages, and a `parse_row(line: &str) -> Result<Row, RowError>` function.
Collect results in a `BTreeMap` (or `HashMap` plus sorting) keyed by student and by subject.
Put the report-building code in its own module (`mod report`).
stretch: Accept an optional fourth column `weight` and compute weighted averages.
